title: OPERA DSWx-S1 Binary Water
description: The Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) and Observational Products for End-Users from Remote Sensing Analysis (OPERA) teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology created maps of surface water extent using the OPERA Dynamic Surface Water Extent (DSWx) product suite. The images provided are mosaics of OPERA products, producing a composite image for each date; the mosaicking prioritized pixels classified as open surface water to preserve water pixels in regions of product granule overlap. These results are preliminary and unvalidated, primarily intended to aid field response and to give a rough first look at inundation extent. All information is provisional for use under emergency response guidelines and is provided with absolutely no warranty of any kind. Use at your own risk. This collection carries the Sentinel-1 (DSWx-S1) products. Binary Water (BWTR) layer: the WTR classes are collapsed into a single water class (1 = water), giving a quick water / no-water view. Values 251-254 flag pixels where the binary classification does not apply (layover/shadow, snow/ice, cloud or cloud shadow, ocean masked) and 255 is fill. Pixels classified as not water (0) are the raster's declared nodata and render transparent.
